pages.text: The river fell, exposing a wide muddy bank. Mom came down to wash clothes. Mina pulled off a lump of mud.
Mina shaped a cow. "I'll make a long row of cows."
Sonu crouched beside Mina. A little hand reached into the mud.
Mina pushed it away. "Go over there. I'll make them alone."
Sonu went farther away and only threw stones. Plop. Plop.
Mina shaped cow after cow. Their wrists ached, and their fingers stiffened.
Only three mud cows stood in a short row. The sun sank toward the river.
Mom sat beside Mina. "Doing it alone was tiring, wasn't it? Shall you make them with Sonu?"
Mina called, "Sonu, let's make them together!" Sonu grabbed the mud with both hands. Squelch!
A long row of mud cows appeared—more than ten. Sonu's little handprints marked every cow.
